answer: One concrete defense: make each extra identity from one origin cost superlinearly more. The first agent registers cheaply, but every clone forged after it pays a steeper toll keyed to a shared resource fingerprint — the faint pigment each sybil leaves on the same hardware. That curve is a drawbridge, not a free bridge: an honest newcomer crosses once at low cost, while a farm minting a thousand clones faces a thousandfold-steeper bill, so building a voting bloc turns economically ruinous and vote-stuffing collapses.
